title: The Signal of the Deep
premise: Hazel Eriksen, a clone imprinted with the murdered original's memories, arrives at Meridian Deep to close a colony everyone in the Core has written off. While recording the settlement's slow collapse, she discovers an unfamiliar name — Callum Voss — on the manifest of a ship that never flew, and finds him alive in the flooded lower decks, carrying a message encoded in the original Hazel's final memories. The message proves the war between the Core and the Outer Reach was manufactured by the shipping consortium that abandoned Meridian. As the jump window closes, Hazel must choose between delivering the truth and protecting Callum, whom she has come to love against every duty she was grown for; she broadcasts the message, igniting a reckoning rather than a war, and stays behind as the colony's last witness.
about_author: Marguerite Winterbourne is a former marine archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned station records before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the North Atlantic coast, where she claims the fog improves her endings.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dead Things
chapters.summary: Hazel Eriksen wakes aboard the transport Kestrel, reviewing the memories of the original Hazel — murdered eleven months ago on Meridian Deep. POV: Hazel. She rehearses being someone else while the colony's last transmission plays on loop. Emotional beat: grief worn like borrowed clothing.

chapters.title: Arrival at Meridian Deep
chapters.summary: Hazel lands at the dying orbital colony, greeted by Administrator Okafor and a population of two hundred holdouts. POV: Hazel. The original's murder case is officially closed, but nothing here matches the memories. Emotional beat: uncanny displacement — home that isn't hers.

chapters.title: Two Hundred People Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Hazel records the colony's decline for the Core archive: failing hydroponics, a reactor on borrowed time, children born who've never seen open sky. POV: Hazel, with engineer Sefa as guide. Emotional beat: tenderness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: In the original's sealed office, Hazel finds the passenger manifest of the ship Perihelion — listed as never launched — bearing a name absent from every database: Callum Voss. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Hazel interrogates her inherited memories and realizes the original had redacted her own recollections before death — deliberately. POV: Hazel. A memory fragment surfaces: a locked deck below the waterline. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own mind.

chapters.title: Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: Hazel descends into the flooded lower decks alone, past drowned corridors the administration pretends don't exist. POV: Hazel. She finds the Perihelion docked and pressurized — and a man alive inside it. Emotional beat: dread transmuting into wonder.

chapters.title: Callum Voss
chapters.summary: Callum, a courier who stowed away six years ago, explains he's been hiding from the consortium's enforcers who killed the original Hazel to bury what he carries. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: wary recognition — he knew the original, and grieves the copy.

chapters.title: A Message Written in Someone Else's Death
chapters.summary: Callum reveals the message is encoded in the original Hazel's final memories — which only her clone can fully read. POV: alternating Hazel/Callum. Emotional beat: the horrible intimacy of being the key to a dead woman's secret.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Administrator Okafor confronts Hazel: he knows about Callum, and reveals the Core pays him to keep the colony's true casualty numbers quiet. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: a decent man complicit in erasure.

chapters.title: Decoding the Drowned Years
chapters.summary: Working in the Perihelion's darkened bridge, Hazel and Callum decode fragments: shipping manifests proving the consortium manufactured the border incident that started the war. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: fury kindling under methodical calm.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Sefa reports the next jump window to the Core opens in nine days and won't recur for fourteen months — and the reactor may not last that long. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: the clock begins.

chapters.title: Enforcers in the Hydroponics Bay
chapters.summary: Consortium enforcers arrive under cover of a resupply run, hunting the manifest leak. Hazel hides Callum; a holdout teenager is detained in his place. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening duty into something dangerous.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Trapped together during a hull breach drill gone wrong, Hazel and Callum speak plainly: she is not the woman he mourned, and he is not the mission. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love admitted as a complication neither will renounce.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Night
chapters.summary: Decoding unlocks the original's final memory intact: she chose death over surrendering Callum, and left a personal addendum addressed 'to whoever I become.' POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: blessing and burden from her former self.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: Okafor offers Hazel a deal: hand over Callum, and the Core evacuates all two hundred colonists before the reactor fails. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of mercy.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Lives or One Truth
chapters.summary: Hazel weighs the trade; the colonists themselves vote to refuse evacuation bought with silence. POV: Hazel, with Sefa and the holdouts. Emotional beat: belonging found — these strangers claim her as theirs.

chapters.title: The Enforcers Breach the Perihelion
chapters.summary: Enforcers storm the hidden ship; Callum is captured, and the decoded evidence is seized — except the copy embedded in Hazel's own memory. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: despair, then the realization of what she carries.

chapters.title: Everything I Was Grown For
chapters.summary: Hazel walks into the enforcer command post offering herself and the full memory in exchange for Callum and the colonists' safety — knowing they'll wipe her. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen without melodrama.

chapters.title: Broadcast Before the Window Closes
chapters.summary: In the chaos of the exchange, Sefa hijacks the colony's transmitter array: Hazel's memory-broadcast floods every Core channel with the consortium's crime as the jump window opens. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: triumph through collective defiance.

chapters.title: The War That Didn't Start
chapters.summary: Core fleets stand down mid-deployment; consortium executives are arrested; the enforcers, unpaid and exposed, release Callum. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: the strange anticlimax of a war ending with paperwork and shame.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Evacuation ships arrive — voluntary this time. Hazel, partially wiped by the enforcers' attempt, has lost chunks of the original but kept her own year. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from lived days rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: The Signal of the Deep
chapters.summary: Hazel chooses to stay as Meridian's recorder-in-residence; Callum stays too, no longer hiding. Her first new entry: not a record of death, but of a colony choosing to live. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
